meaning: Models that read cameras and joint sensors and decide what a machine's motors do next.
The arm that does the task; it copies the leader during teaching and later runs the policy.
A second, matching arm a person moves by hand to steer the follower.
One recorded attempt at the task: a table of joint readings and motor commands over time, plus video from each camera.
The model that maps what the robot senses to what it does next.
A model that predicts what happens next, given what the robot sees and an action it might take.
A program that steps a virtual copy of the arm and its scene through physics and draws what virtual cameras would see.
Decoding recorded video, dropping bad episodes and removing near-duplicates before training.
Making more training samples from the recorded ones, from image changes to generated video.
One job in the loop that fills one part of the machine first; the dive counts fifteen.
A piece of a computer that saturates separately from the others, such as CPU cores or a GPU's tensor cores.
The GPU's units for matrix arithmetic, used by training and inference.
Separate GPU units that follow light rays to draw an image.
Fixed circuits on a GPU that only compress and decompress video.
The rate at which memory can stream data to the processor.
How long one unit runs, whether its pieces exchange data while running, and whether it can be stopped and resumed.
A compact learned summary of a scene that a model predicts in place of pixels.
A model design that predicts the latent of what comes next instead of its pixels.
A policy that also reads a written instruction alongside camera images.
Training by trial and reward.
Moving a policy trained in simulation onto the real arm.
Many robots managed together.
The event counters built into a processor that show where its cycles go.
